evidence.claim: Transaction 3523199 for $100.07 on card C02923-K1 scored risk_score 0.54 via online channel on a new iOS device with mismatched billing and registered emails.
Only 1 transaction occurred in the 2-hour window around the flagged transaction, indicating no burst testing.
Card history shows predominantly in-person transactions in region 330.0; the flagged online transaction is an anomaly.
The new device profile was shared across 4 cards belonging to 4 distinct customers (C08299, C07987, C02923, C02354).
Card C02923-K1 shares multiple device profiles with other connected cards including C08299-K1, C03042-K1, and C12265-K2.
Three similar closed cases matching card_not_present_new_device at ~$100 exposure all resulted in confirmed fraud.
Fraud probability >= 0.3 requires opening a case.
SAR filing required when fraud confirmed or strongly suspected (p >= 0.7) and activity connects to shared device or another customer's fraud.
Stop investigation when p >= 0.85 with >= 2 independent pieces of evidence.

case.summary: Transaction 3523199 ($100.07) flagged at risk_score 0.54. Investigation revealed it occurred on a new device shared by 4 different customers' cards, deviating from the cardholder's typical in-person pattern. Three identical historical cases were confirmed fraud. Fraud probability assessed at 0.85. Case closed as fraud with SAR filed due to multi-customer device sharing.

sar.reason: Fraud strongly suspected (p=0.85) and activity connects to a shared device used by multiple customers, satisfying §3a criteria.
sar.narrative: Transaction 3523199 for $100.07 on card C02923-K1 was identified as fraudulent. The transaction occurred online via a new iOS device that was also used by three other customers (C08299, C07987, C02354), indicating coordinated card-not-present fraud using a shared device. Historical precedent cases CC-0117, CC-3539, and CC-1588 with identical patterns and amounts were previously confirmed as fraud.

stop_reason: §6 stop: p >= 0.85 reached with multiple independent pieces of evidence (new device, multi-customer sharing, historical precedents).
